overview: BCAP trains an adversarial generator with one extra critic loss: a squared penalty whenever the critic input-gradient norm exceeds a threshold, evaluated separately on real and generated data. The simple family uses native Adam at constant rates, with no clipping, A2 damping or additive training noise.
symbols: G is the generator; D is the raw-score critic; P is the learnable prior; x is real data; z is a prior sample; y=G(z) is generated data. mean averages samples, norm is the per-sample L2 norm, relu(a)=max(a,0), softplus(a)=log(1+exp(a)). lambda is penalty strength and kappa its gradient-norm threshold. stop_gradient freezes a value for the current update.
pseudocode: Choose an adversarial loss and constant Adam learning rates for G, D and P.
Sample real x and latent z from P; compute y=G(z).
For penalty derivatives, detach samples from G and treat them as differentiable critic inputs; the penalty updates D only.
Backpropagate the critic objective and take a native Adam step on D.
With D fixed, resample latent z, recompute differentiable fake y and scores; backpropagate adversarial_G + task-owned auxiliary losses.
Take native Adam steps on G and trainable prior locations P (and encoder E on joint hosts).
On joint encoder/generator hosts, reverse labels on both critic streams so E also receives a gradient.

training_details.loss: Selectable paired relativistic logistic (canonical/default), non-saturating logistic, hinge, Wasserstein or least squares. The scalar losses are minimized. Relativistic D: mean softplus(D(fake)-D(real)); G reverses the difference. Joint hosts use the explicit generator/encoder objective.
training_details.optimizer: Native PyTorch Adam. Canonical beta1=0, beta2=0.999 and epsilon=1e-8; moments are constant.
training_details.learning_rates: Constant: canonical global LR 0.00425, D multiplier 1 and prior multiplier 2. The measured round also tested global LR 0.0010625. Network and prior LR floors are 1, so the scheduled API path performs no annealing.
training_details.gradient_clipping: None. Critic spike guard is disabled; BCAP acts through the loss, not parameter-gradient clipping.
training_details.critic_penalty: Fixed real/fake one-sided squared L2 cap. Canonical lambda=1, kappa=1, applied every critic update. No K3P early/late blend or critic-anchor term.
training_details.damping_and_guards: No A2 latent-row damping, direct-particle response gain, or adaptive critic step intervention.
training_details.noise: No additive critic-input or generator-output training noise. Sampling noise inherent to a task-declared MoG prior remains part of that prior, not an extra BCAP intervention.
training_details.averaging: Canonical generator EMA decay=0 and no critic-anchor penalty; the reported round scores clean live weights.

configuration_notes: The pseudocode describes the family mechanism; the selected configuration and each task determine architectures, initialization, prior, sampling, update count and task-owned auxiliary losses.
The cap is a soft penalty on gradients with respect to critic inputs, not a hard bound on model-parameter gradients. Its L2 norm is not divided by input dimension.
Configuration alternatives are complete recipes; passing cells from different recipes or sources are not combined.

The original v1 non-relativistic joint-host implementations omitted the encoder-side adversarial term. Corrected v2 candidates use joint_g_loss; original receipts and source identities remain historical evidence.
The family ID remains bcap-pure and the public recipe preset is get_recipe("bcap"). The report label BCAP distinguishes it from BCAP with K3P.

references.title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
references.component: Base optimizer. Repository-specific guards and damping are separate mechanisms.

references.title: The relativistic discriminator: a key element missing from standard GAN
references.component: Paired relativistic logistic objective; this implementation pairs scores, rather than subtracting batch-average scores.

references.title: On the regularization of Wasserstein GANs
references.component: Related work on one-sided gradient penalties. The repository BCAP kernel uses real/fake inputs directly and is not a reproduction of this paper or its sampling scheme.

references.title: Wasserstein GAN
references.component: Wasserstein score-loss option. This BCAP recipe does not adopt the paper’s weight clipping or full training algorithm.

references.title: Least Squares Generative Adversarial Networks
references.component: Least-squares loss option; repository targets are real=1, fake=0 and generator=1.

references.title: Spectral Normalization for Generative Adversarial Networks
references.component: Reference for the hinge adversarial objective option; selecting hinge does not itself enable spectral normalization.
